qâlum: UNCERTAIN: to give heed, pay attention (Harper’s QALU “to give attention to”, written with the sign gul): liqūlma (li-gul-ma, precative, “let him pay heed, and”), iqūlma (i-gul-ma, preterite, “he has paid heed, and”; lā iqūlma “and has not heeded”); the root and the vowels are not settled, and the sense is Harper’s
kibsum: way, tread, procedure (Harper’s kibsu, from kabāsum “to tread”): kibsam (ki-ib-sa-am, accusative) “the way”
ṣalmum-black: black, dark: ṣalmāt (ṣa-al-ma-at, plural before a genitive) in ṣalmāt qaqqadim “the black-headed people” (Harper: “Black-Head race, i.e. mankind”), the phrase of the prologue spelt out in syllables
ela: UNCERTAIN: perhaps ēla “except, apart from” (e-la), a guess from the spelling; Harper prints a footnote with another reading and the stretch is unread
laḫa: UNREAD: la-ḫa, a word Harper gives as bare signs; no meaning is claimed
ZI.IM.RI.GA: UNREAD: four signs Harper prints in capitals without a reading; no meaning is claimed
tanādātum: UNCERTAIN: tanādātim (ta-na-da-tim, genitive) “might, tyranny” (Harper’s tanatu, the d spelled for t); the reading and the sense are unsettled
bêlum-Š: UNCERTAIN: Š-stem of Harper’s bêlu III “to overrule” (not the noun bēlum “lord”): uštepiel (uš-te-pi-el) “he has overruled (set aside)”, said of the king’s words; the root, the vowels and the tense of the spelling are not settled, and the sense is Harper’s
arākum-D: D-stem of arākum “to be long” (Harper’s ARIKU II,1 “to prolong”): lirrik (li-ir-ri-ik, precative) “let him lengthen”, said of the scepter
irritum: curse (Harper’s irritu): irrītīya (ir-ri-ti-ia) “my curses” (with -ia “my”) · irrīt (ir-ri-it, the form before a genitive) “the curse of” · irrītim (ir-ri-tim, genitive) “of the curse”: aššum irrītim šināti “because of these curses”
mašûm: to forget (Harper’s masu I,1): imēšma (i-me-eš-ma, preterite + -ma) “he has forgotten, and”
adārum: to fear, be afraid (Harper’s adaru): idūrma (i-dur-ma, preterite + -ma) “he has feared, and”; lā idūrma “and has not feared”
pasāsum-D: D-stem of pasāsum “to blot out, abolish” (Harper’s pasasu II,2): uptassis (up-ta-az-zi-is, D perfect, the double s written with z) “he has blotted out”
pašāṭum: to efface, rub out (Harper’s pasatu I,1): ipšiṭma (ip-ši-iṭ-ma, preterite + -ma) “he has erased, and”
patesi: governor, ruler of a city (the Sumerian title PA.TE.SI, which Harper keeps as pa-te-si); written PA.TE.SI with three signs and said patesi
awīlūtum: mankind, a person, the human race (Harper’s awilutu): awīlūtum (a-wi-lu-tum) in lū … ù lū awīlūtum “or any person”
palûm: reign, term of rule (the BAL sign, Harper’s List no. 7, palû): palêya (BALA-ia, with -ia “my”) “my reign” · palê (BALA, before a genitive) “the reign of”: palê tanēḫim “a reign of sighing”
arārum: to curse (Harper’s araru I,1): lirur (li-ru-ur, precative) “let him curse”
šâmum-D: D-stem of šâmum “to fix, decide” (Harper’s samu II,1): mušīm (mu-ši-im, D participle before a genitive) “one who fixes”: mušīm šīmātim “who fixes the fates”
rabûm-Š: Š-stem of rabûm “to be great” (Harper’s rabu III,1 “to enlarge, make great”): mušarbû (mu-šar-bu-u, Š participle) “one who makes great”: mušarbû šarrūtīya “who makes my kingship great”
tēšûm: UNCERTAIN: revolt, uproar (Harper’s tešu “revolt”): tēšī (te-ši, said with a long ī; the case ending in the construct is not known) in a phrase that is itself uncertain
šabûm-D: UNCERTAIN: Harper’s šabu II,1 “to attack, to control”: šubbîm (šu-ub-bi-im) in tēšī lā šubbîm “a revolt not to be controlled (?)”; the form and the sense are unsettled
raḫlum: UNCERTAIN: curse (Harper’s raḫlu): raḫ (ra-aḫ) in qāssu raḫ “his hand, a curse (?)”; the form is cut short and its place in the sentence is unclear
tanēḫum: sighing, groaning (Harper’s taneḫu): tanēḫim (ta-ne-ḫi-im, genitive) in palê tanēḫim “a reign of sighing”
iṣûm: small, few (Harper’s isu “small”, written i-zu-tim with ZU for ṣu): iṣūtim (feminine plural) in ūmī iṣūtim “few days”; “few” is the sense that fits the line
ḫušaḫḫum: hunger, famine (Harper’s ḫušaḫḫu): ḫušaḫḫim (ḫu-ša-aḫ-ḫi-im, genitive) in šanāt ḫušaḫḫim “years of famine”
ekletum: darkness (Harper’s eklitu): eklit (ik-li-it) in eklit lā nawārim “darkness without light”
mūtum: death (mūtum; not mutum “husband”): mūt (mu-ut, the form before a genitive) “death of”
nīṭilum: UNCERTAIN: look, glance (Harper’s nitlu “look, staring”): nīṭil (ni-ṭi-il, the form before a genitive) in mūt nīṭil īnim “death of a glance of the eye (?)”; the force of the phrase is unsettled
sapāḫum-N: N-stem of sapāḫum “to scatter” (Harper’s sapahu IV,1 “to be dispersed”): našpuḫ (na-aš-pu-uḫ) “the scattering”, a verbal noun before a genitive, našpuḫ nišīšu “the scattering of his people”
Bēlit: Bēlit, “the lady”, the goddess, consort of Bêl (Harper’s Bêlit [NIN.LIL], written with the star, NIN and KID): the name is Harper’s reading of the sign group, not a spelling met in the text
kabātum: to be heavy, be weighty, be potent (Harper’s kabatu I,1): kabtat (kab-ta-at, stative, 3rd feminine) “she is weighty”: ša kibīssa ina Ekur kabtat “whose command is weighty in Ekur”
šipṭum: judgment (Harper’s šiptu): šipṭim (ši-ip-di-im, genitive, DI written for ṭi) in ašar šipṭim ù purussîm “the place of judgment and decision”
lemēnum-D: D-stem of lemēnum “to be evil” (Harper’s limenu II,1 “to be evil, hostile”): lilemmin (li-li-mi-in, precative) “let her make evil”
lapātum-Š: Š-stem of lapātum “to smite, overturn” (Harper’s lapatu III,1): šulpūt (šu-ul-pu-ut, verbal noun before a genitive) “the overthrow of”: šulpūt mātišu “the overthrow of his land”
tabākum: to pour out (Harper’s tabaku): tabāk (ta-ba-ak, infinitive before a genitive) “the pouring out of”: tabāk napištišu “the pouring out of his life”
šakānum-Š: Š-stem of šakānum “to set, place”: lišaškin (li-ša-aš-ki-in, precative) “let her cause to be set”, said of a curse laid on a man

__broaden__.diānum: to judge: dīnam idīn “he judged a case” · adīnu (a-di-nu) “I judged” (first person preterite + relative -u, filed by Harper under dânum “to judge”; the same word was read addinu, nadānum, in the part before): dīn adīnu “the verdict I judged” · lidīn (li-di-in, precative) “let him judge”
__broaden__.purussûm: decision, verdict · purussâšina (pu-ru-za-ši-na, accusative singular + -šina “their”, the double s written with ZA) “their decision” · purussê (pu-ru-us-se-e) “decisions of” · purussîm (genitive) “of the decision”
__broaden__.kittum: truth, right — kittum u mīšarum, “truth and justice” · kīnātim (ki-na-tim, plural) “truths”: Šamaš kīnātim išrukušum “Shamash gave him truths”
__broaden__.Enlil: Enlil ({d}EN.LÍL) — lord of the lands, chief of the pantheon’s executive · said Ellil, written {d}EN.LÍL (the star + EN + KID), which Harper prints as Bêl “lord” (his glossary BEL [EN.LIL]); also Ellil šarrim “Ellil the king”
__broaden__.emqum: wise, skilled · imkim (im-ki-im, Harper’s IM-KI-IM (?)): perhaps imqim “of the wise one”, UNCERTAIN, the reading is the drafter’s suggestion and not Harper’s
__broaden__.ilum: god; here: the temple as owner · plural ilāni “gods” (written DINGIR.DINGIR, as in the litany): maḫar ilāni “before the gods” · ilum (the AN sign alone, DINGIR) “the god”, the god not named in the line · ilī (written NI.NI, two triangle signs, Harper’s List no. 99) “gods”: irrīt ilī “the curse of the gods”, abu ilī “father of the gods”
__broaden__.bēltum: lady, mistress (the feminine of bēlum): bēltiša (be-el-ti-ša) “her mistress”; bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”, from the construct bēlit + -ša, t + š said ss · bēltum written with the single sign NIN, “lady”
__broaden__.egirrûm: UNCERTAIN: Harper’s egirru “dreams, plans”, the sense in this line unclear: igirrê (i-gi-ir-ri-e, plural, oblique case) · igirrīya (with -ia “my”) “my igirrû” (plans? dreams?), UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.kibītum: speech, command (Harper’s kibitu): kibīt (ki-be-it, the form before a genitive) “command of” · kibīssu (ki-be-zu, with -šu “his”) “his command”; kibīssa (ki-be-za, with -ša “her”) “her command”; the ss is written with ZU and ZA
__broaden__.rêʾûm-pasture: to pasture, graze (a herd): the infinitive in the genitive after ana, ana … rēʾîm “to pasture” (ri-im), said rēʾîm; the spelling ri-im is Harper’s and the reading of the word as the infinitive of rêʾûm (the verb behind rēʾûm “shepherd”) is my own from the grammar, UNCERTAIN · lirʾi (li-ri, precative) “let him shepherd”: nišīšu ina mīšarim lirʾi “let him shepherd his people in justice”; the spelling li-ri has no sign for the ʾ, and Harper files it under another verb (ARU II,1 “to carry, to rule”), so the reading is UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.wabālum-Š: Š-stem of wabālum “to carry”: to make carry off, let (water) carry away: uštābil (perfect) “he has let (the water) carry off” · ušābilšu (u-ša-bil-šu, preterite) “he had (him) carry”; šūbulu (šu-bu-lu, Š stative šūbul with the subjunctive -u) “(what) has been sent”, šūbulūma (šu-bu-lu-ma) “has been sent, and”; the stative reading is from the form and the exact sense is UNCERTAIN · ušābil (u-ša-bi-il) “he has had (a present) brought” (preterite, without -u where there is no ša); ušābilu (u-ša-bi-lu) “who had (a present) brought” (with the relative -u) · šūbilam (šu-bi-lam) “the carrying off (?)”: šarrūssu šūbilam “the carrying off (?) of his kingship”; Harper enters it under abalu III,1 “to bring, to take away, to transport”, but the vowels are not those of the infinitive, so the form is UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.bašûm-Š: Š-stem of bašûm “to exist”: to bring into being, produce (a crop): uštabši “he has produced” (perfect) · uštabši (uš-tab-ši) “he has brought about” (perfect): kazzatam uštabši “he has brought about a harm (?)” · ušabšû (u-ša-ab-šu-u) “which he brought about” (preterite + relative -u) · šubšâm (su-ub-sa-a-am, Š infinitive) “to bring into being”: lā šubšâm “not to be brought into being”, Harper’s basu III,1, with no sense given by him
__broaden__.nasāḫum: to pull out, uproot; of a son, to cast out, disinherit (Harper: “to cut off, to disinherit”): nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im, infinitive) “to cast out”; anassaḫ (a-na-za-aḫ) “I shall cast out” (first person present); inassaḫ (i-na-za-aḫ) “he shall cast out” (third person present) · inassaḫū (i-na-za-ḫu) “they shall pluck out”, present plural: īnšu inassaḫū “they shall pluck out his eye” (the ZA sign for sa) · nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im) infinitive “to cast out”: ana tarbītim nasāḫim “to cast out the foster-child” · assuḫ (az-zu-uḫ, preterite, 1st person) “I tore out”, of enemies · lissuḫ (li-zu-uḫ, precative, the n assimilated and the ss written with ZU) “let him uproot”: raggam u ṣēnam lissuḫ “let him uproot the wicked and the evil one”
__broaden__.ḫaṭṭum: scepter · written GIŠ.PA-šu, said ḫaṭṭašu “his scepter”
__broaden__.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease) · ūm “day” (UD), before a following word, in ūm NER lā “a day (when ?) NER not …” · ūmīšu (UD-mi-šu) “his days”: ūmīšu imannûma “they shall count his days” · ina ūmim (i-na UD) “per day, by the day”, with the numeral 1{kam}: ina ūmim 1{kam} 180 qa “for each day 180 qa”; the day-rate formula of §271–277 · ūmī (the sign UD alone) “days”: ūmī iṣūtim “few days”
__broaden__.qātum: hand: ina qāt “from the hand of” · qātīšu (qa₂-ti-šu) “of his hands”: bīš qātīšu “his own goods” · qāt (qa₂-at) construct “in the hand of, in the care of”: ina qāt mušēniqtim “in the care (hand) of the wet-nurse” · qātīšu “of his hands” in šipir qātīšu “the work of his hands” · ina qātišu (qa₂-ti-šu) “in his hand”: ittaṣbat ina qātišu “he was caught with it in his hand” · qāssu (qa₂-zu, with -šu “his”, the ss written with ZU) “his hand”
__broaden__.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · uttēr (ut-te-ir, perfect) “he has given back”: the same verb as utâr · litēršu (li-te-ir-šu, precative + -šu, Harper’s taru II,1) “let him turn back / take back from him”, UNCERTAIN: litēršu šarrūtam “let him turn the glory of kingship away from him”
__broaden__.damāqum-D: D-stem of damāqum “to be good”: to show favor, be gracious (Harper’s damaku II “to favor”): lidammiqū (li-dam-mi-qu₂, precative, 3rd plural, KU read qu₂) “may they show favor” · mudammiqat (mu-dam-mi-qa₂-at, D participle, feminine) “she who makes good, who favors”: bēltum mudammiqat igirrīya “the lady who makes my igirrû favorable”
